findings.passage: When Kit Connor reminded him in 2026, "You taught me how to misbehave on a film set," Harries answered, "I may have taken the license to be silly and run with it."
findings.problem: The exchange runs the other way round in Interview (S02). Connor says they 'could be silly, which I’ve tried to carry forward and learn from you'. Harries replies 'I may have taken the license to be silly and run with it.' Only then does Connor add 'You taught me how to misbehave on a film set.' The article presents Harries's line as an answer to a line Connor said afterwards. The C21 claim text repeats the reversal.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence follows the order in the source, for example: 'When Kit Connor said in 2026 that he had learned to be silly on set from him, Harries answered, "I may have taken the license to be silly and run with it." "You taught me how to misbehave on a film set," Connor added.' C21 is updated to match, and its passage still matches the article.

findings.passage: On release day, when a Three would feel most exposed, he told Cultured, "I went through a phase of being nervous,"
findings.problem: Cultured (S03) published the interview on October 23, 2026, but the question he answered was 'How are you feeling a couple days out from Clayface’s release?'. He said this a couple of days before release, not on release day. C66 has the same error ('On release day (2026-10-23) he told Cultured'). The argument still works, since the pre-release window is a fair point to test reception anxiety, but the timing is stated wrongly.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence dates the remark accurately, for example 'A couple of days before release, when a Three would feel most exposed, he told Cultured...' or 'In a Cultured interview published on release day...'. C66 is corrected to match, and its passage still matches the article.

findings.passage: "I played Elden Ring to switch my brain off during the three months I was screen testing for Clayface," he told Connor. "It probably talks to my level of anxiety throughout that period."
findings.problem: Two of his lines are joined as if one continuous statement. In S02, Connor's remark ('That’s a tough game to switch your brain off to, but probably actually the perfect one, too') comes between them, and 'It' refers to picking such a hard game. The joined version slightly changes what 'it' refers to: choosing that particular game, not the act of escaping.
findings.acceptance_test: The two lines are separated with the intervening context, for example: '...he told Connor. When Connor said it was a tough game to switch off to, Harries answered, "It probably talks to my level of anxiety throughout that period."' C04 records the join.

findings.passage: and his favorite escape, fixing motorbikes, is about certainty
findings.problem: The FAQ adds precision the source does not give. Square Mile (S01) has him saying 'I love doing manual stuff', that he has 'ridden bikes for years' but his bike 'conked out at the start of the pandemic and I just never replaced it', and that it is 'like an antidote'. Nothing calls it his favorite escape, and 'fixing' is only implied by 'manual stuff'. The body's wording ('the escape he describes most fondly', 'working on motorbikes') is closer to the source. The body's 'He plays guitar and rides motorbikes' (2022: no current bike) is similarly loose.
findings.acceptance_test: The FAQ says something like 'the escape he describes most fondly, motorbikes, is about certainty', or otherwise drops the 'favorite' superlative. Optionally, 'rides motorbikes' becomes 'has ridden motorbikes for years' (2022).
